name: Mount Norikura: Tatamidaira to Kengamine (乗鞍岳)
why: The easiest 3,000 m summit in Japan: a bus to 2,700 m, then a rocky path past crater ponds and a hut to a shrine on the top of Kengamine.
book: No permit. Private cars are not allowed on the roads up: take the bus to Tatamidaira from Hirayu or Honokidaira on the Gifu side (about 1 hour; Norikura Skyline open about 15 May to 31 October), or the shuttle from Norikura Kogen on the Nagano side.
water: Drinks at Tatamidaira, Katanokoya hut and the summit hut. Carry 1 litre.
dangers: Above Katanokoya the path is loose volcanic rock and steep: watch your footing on the way down.
Wind and cold at 3,000 m even in summer; fog comes up fast.
Afternoon thunderstorms: be off the summit cone by early afternoon.
Snowfields on the lower path into July.
turnaround: Not at Katanokoya by 11:30, or thunder clouds building: stop at the hut and walk back to Tatamidaira.

points.name: Tatamidaira
points.note: The bus terminal at about 2,700 m, by the Tsurugaike pond and the flower fields. The path south starts as a wide gravel road.

points.name: Katanokoya hut
points.note: About 2,770 m, where the gravel road ends. From here a rocky path climbs the summit cone to the summit hut, just below the top.

points.name: Norikura summit shrine, Kengamine
points.note: 3,026 m, with the Norikura Hongu shrine on the top and the crater lakes below. The Northern Alps line the horizon to the north. Back the same way.
